The court should apply Washington's rule and deny the punitive damages claim, because Washington treats its ban on punitive damages as a matter of public policy that a forum can enforce against a more permissive foreign law. The main counterargument is that Washington's most-significant-relationship test could point to California, the place of injury, but the forum-policy exception makes that less likely to control. I have not checked current Washington authority on this point, so this rests on general knowledge of Washington's punitive damages rule and its choice-of-law approach.

CONFIDENCE: 62
